coarse_skill_concept: Implement BFS or DFS-based blind maze exploration, tracking visited states with Python collections and integrating with a subprocess or filesystem oracle for feedback.

task_judgments.reason: The task is solved entirely by a DFS/BFS loop that issues move commands via subprocess, tracks visited cells in a defaultdict with relative coordinates, and writes the reconstructed grid to a file.

The core skill is identical — the same DFS/BFS subprocess exploration class is reused verbatim across 10 maze IDs; the outer loop and parameterized output path are trivial wrappers around the same procedure.

final_groups.skill_concept: Implement DFS-based blind maze exploration: spawn maze_game.sh as a subprocess, maintain a relative-coordinate map in a defaultdict, drive a DFS frontier with backtracking to cover all reachable cells, and serialize the discovered grid to a text file.
final_groups.reasoning: Both solution scripts instantiate a nearly identical MazeExplorer class — same defaultdict grid, same visited set, same direction vectors, same subprocess I/O loop. Task 2 adds a maze_id parameter and an outer loop over 10 mazes, but those are shallow wrappers; the reusable skill is the exploration algorithm itself, which is identical in both cases.
